description: Plan v7 section 8.3 fixture family 'owed-m3b-member-statics'. Inputs only; the oracle emits expected.

cases.notes: A wildcard-free PRIVATE-USE range. Every private-use range already in the corpus (x-*, x-foo-*) carries a wildcard, so nothing had shown what a bare one does. DISCRIMINATION: a private-use member gets no canonicalRange, no canonicalRangeSubtags, no fallbackChainCanonicalTags, no requestedLikelyLanguageScript and semanticDepth 0 (DefaultStrings$MemberStatics.<init>:3051 else arm), which structurally disables every derived rung. A port that computed those statics would hold canonicalRangeSubtags [x, lokal] and reach the loaded x-lokal-a catalog by prefix truncation, exactly as en reaches en-US. Java selects nothing.

The positive half of the same discrimination, so the observable difference is a SELECTION rather than an absence: the private-use member is listed FIRST at equal weight and Java still selects fr. A port that derived a match for x-lokal from canonical statics would answer x-lokal-a instead.

The guard against overcorrecting: withholding the canonical/fallback-chain precomputation must not make a private-use range unmatchable. The exact spelling of the loaded private-use catalog still selects it EXACTLY, so a port that answered NONE for every private-use range fails here while passing the two rows above.

An undetermined range with a REGION attached, which is where the withheld statics bite hardest: CLDR's likely subtag for und-US is en-Latn, so a port that computed requestedLikelyLanguageScript and the fallback chain for this member would reach the loaded en-US catalog. Java computes none of them and selects nothing. The corpus's only prior undetermined range (und-latn) is bare, so nothing had shown that the undetermined refusal survives an attached region that would otherwise resolve.

One member of each shape in a single list, all at equal weight, with the ordinary member LAST. Java answers fr. A port that computed statics for either special member answers en-US (from und-US, via likely subtag en-Latn) or x-lokal-a (from x-lokal, via prefix truncation) instead, so this row separates the arms twice over. FINDING recorded while authoring it: this list cannot cover the private-use conjunct of DefaultStrings$MemberStatics.<init>:3051, because CldrLocaleData.TagParts.forLanguageTag sets privateUse=true only on its startsWith("x-") early return, and that same return sets language="" -- so privateUse implies undetermined and the third conjunct is unreachable in the true direction. That disposition is now excluded, not owed.
